overview: Black develops with 2...e6, so the bishop on g5 is not hit at once. White usually plays 3.e4 h6 4.Bxf6 Qxf6 5.Nc3 for a big centre against the bishop pair, or the quieter 3.Nd2 and 3.Nc3, 3.e3. Black aims to undermine the centre with ...d6/...c5/...e5 and use the two bishops; White aims to keep space and avoid being opened up.

white_ideas.idea: e4 and d4 centre after Bxf6, with Nc3 and Nf3
Nd2 and e3 set-up, keeping the bishop on g5 or h4

black_ideas.idea: Strike at the centre with ...c5 or ...d6 and ...e5

typical_structures.structure: White e4-d4 centre against Black's bishop pair after Bxf6 Qxf6
Queen's-pawn structure with e3 and c3 when White keeps the bishop

character.notes: 3.e4 h6 4.Bxf6 Qxf6 gives an imbalanced but not forcing middlegame; the quieter lines are calm.

gambit.notes: No pawn offered in the main lines.

soundness.notes: All the main lines are playable for both sides.

structure.notes: Centre is tense or still forming (d4/e4 against ...d6/...c5), not locked and not clearly open.

approach.notes: Bg5 against 1...Nf6 is a favourite of a few specialists, but it is a standard choice in the sense that strong players use it; it is not played against everything.

level.notes: Plans are clear, little to memorise, but the bishop pair against the big centre takes judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Trompowsky: 2...e6 3.e4 h6 4.Bxf6 Qxf6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bg5 e6 3. e4 h6 4. Bxf6
sublines_that_differ.how: Main line of the root: White's centre against the bishop pair.

character.reason: Imbalanced pieces but neither side is forced into sharp play.

soundness.reason: Both sides' main lines are fully playable.

structure.reason: Centre is not yet resolved and varies by branch.

approach.reason: Played by strong players against one reply, not a universal set-up.

level.reason: Few lines to learn but handling the bishop pair takes judgement.

plans.reason: Black gets the bishop pair, White the space.
